sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports the snapshot type
sections.what: Brings in the definition of one imagery record so the file knows which fields a snapshot must have.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the data format checked by the type system.

sections.name: ImageryProvider
sections.title: Imagery source contract and snapshot builder
sections.what: Defines the shape any imagery source must follow, which is one method that returns snapshots for a case. It also has a helper that builds one snapshot with fixed labels: synthetic provider, fixture source, demo-only quality and not authoritative.
sections.why: Likely reason: every record gets the same warning labels so none can pass as official.
sections.watch_out: Removing or changing these labels would let demo data look like real evidence.

sections.name: fixtures
sections.title: Stored demo imagery for two cases
sections.what: Holds the fixed demo records: two dated snapshots for the hero case with changing vegetation and built-up values, and two stable snapshots for the control case.
sections.why: Likely reason: fixed records let the hero and control stories be compared and tested.
sections.watch_out: The numbers here are also expected by the test file, so edit both together.

sections.name: SyntheticImageryProvider, syntheticImageryProvider
sections.title: Serves a copy of demo imagery
sections.what: Returns the snapshots for a requested case as fresh copies, or nothing if the case has no demo imagery. Copying stops callers from changing the stored originals.
sections.why: Likely reason: copying protects the stored fixtures from accidental edits.
sections.watch_out: Only the metrics object is copied, so any richer nested data added later would be shared unless it is copied too.

summary: Supplies fixed, made-up satellite-style snapshots for the demo cases and labels every one as synthetic and not authoritative.
purpose: Gives the demo a way to show land change over two dates (vegetation and built-up change) without calling a real imagery service.
why: Likely reason: a demo needs predictable data, and the labels stop anyone from treating it as official evidence.
how: The fixtures table holds two snapshots for the hero case and two for the control case, each built by the snapshot helper. The SyntheticImageryProvider class returns a copy of a case's snapshots, or null when the case has no fixtures. The shared syntheticImageryProvider instance is exported for use elsewhere.
inputs: A case identifier such as the demo case IDs.
outputs: A list of snapshots with date, visual type, change numbers, notes and a synthetic reference link, or null.
risks: If the labels are dropped, demo imagery could be mistaken for real data. Changing a fixture changes what the demo shows.
debug: If the demo shows no imagery, check the case ID exactly matches a key in the fixtures table. If numbers look wrong, compare them with the imagery provider test expectations.
